<p align="center"><img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skizzophrenic/SquachWatch-CYD/v1.7.0/docs/settings-menu.gif" width="640" alt="The settings screen: tapping a group heading folds its rows away, then a second heading folds too, leaving a short menu; BACK sits on the bottom edge throughout."></p>

**Squachy draws about 40% faster, and the settings screen stopped being a scroll.** Everything on screen is the same; it just arrives quicker and you can find it. There is also groundwork here for updating the firmware without a cable, which is the first half of a two-part job.

## He got faster

Squachy's arms, legs and brows are drawn as thick lines, and the display library was drawing every one of them the slow way: a floating-point distance calculation for each pixel, then reading the screen back to blend the edges. One Squachy cost 28 milliseconds. The screen only takes 23 to push.

Drawing those same lines as plain filled shapes takes 3.4 milliseconds, and nobody can tell the difference by looking, because the emulator every approved design was checked in has been drawing them the plain way all along.

The clear screen went from about 18 frames a second to 25 or 26.

## The backgrounds hold their speed

Fourteen of the animated backgrounds moved by one step per frame, which meant they ran at whatever speed the board happened to manage. A faster board made the rain fall faster. They now move by elapsed time instead, so the digital rain, the starfield, the aquarium and the fire look the same on every board.

## Settings

**Tap a group heading to fold it away.** BEHAVIOR, SQUACHY and SYSTEM each collapse to a single line, which turns a list four screens deep into something you can see all of.

**BACK is pinned to the bottom edge.** It used to be the last row, so leaving from the middle of the list meant scrolling to the end to find it.

**A SYSTEM page** now holds touch calibration, the colour check, diagnostics and reset stats. They are the four rows you touch once a year and they were sitting below everything you actually adjust.

**Each page remembers where you were.** Step into APPEARANCE and back out and you land where you left, not at the top.

**Boring mode greys its rows instead of hiding them,** with the reason where the value would be. A hidden row and a row that never existed look identical, so anyone hunting for OUTFIT after switching boring mode on had no way to see where it went. Things you have not unlocked stay hidden completely — a greyed-out row naming a secret would give it away.

## You can stop watching something

Long-pressing a device in the log or the scanner sets a watch on it, and until now there was no way to unset one. The button did not toggle, no screen ever named the target, and the only way out was rebooting.

Now the title bar carries a small WATCH or HUNT badge whenever one is set, tapping it opens the target, and there is a button to stop. The same row appears in settings. HUNT had the identical problem and got the same treatment, including a STOP button on the hunt screen beside BACK — BACK leaves it running, which is the point of having both.

## Room for updates to arrive later

The board's storage is now split into two firmware slots instead of one. A board needs somewhere to receive a new version while still running the old one, and somewhere to fall back to if it fails.

**This release does not update over the air.** It is the release that makes the next one able to. The storage layout is read before the firmware starts, so it can never be changed wirelessly — this one has to go on over USB like every release so far. Your settings, PIN and mesh pairings survive the change.

## Also

The FAQ said thirteen detection types when there are seventeen, and suggested the 3.5" board was worth trying. It boot loops and is not being worked on. Both corrected.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: fold a settings group by tapping its heading
- **Added**: a SYSTEM page for calibration, colours, diagnostics and reset stats
- **Added**: BACK pinned to the bottom of the settings screen
- **Added**: a WATCH/HUNT badge in the title bar, and matching rows in settings
- **Added**: STOP HUNT on the hunt screen and in both long-press panels
- **Added**: two firmware slots, so a later release can arrive over the air
- **Changed**: Squachy's thick lines draw ~8x faster; CLEAR runs at 25-26 fps, up from 18
- **Changed**: fourteen backgrounds now move by elapsed time, so speed matches across boards
- **Changed**: settings pages each remember their scroll position
- **Changed**: boring mode greys its rows with the reason instead of hiding them
- **Changed**: FAQ corrected on detection count, the 3.5" board, and its flasher links
- **Fixed**: a watch or hunt could only be ended by rebooting or wiping the device
